newsitem.title: UK: IPE May Brent ends softer in quiet market.
newsitem.headline: IPE May Brent ends softer in quiet market.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil ended the day softer as selling came into the market in the last 15 minutes bringing the prompt contract into negative territory.
May Brent closed on Tuesday down four cents at $19.55 a barrel.

Brokers said there was little market moving news about and all eyes would focus on the American Petroleum Institute's (API) weekly U.S. petroleum statistics due to be released after markets close on Tuesday.

"From the way the (NYMEX) heating oil led the way up today it looks like someone thinks we are going to see a substantial draw there (in API's) so we'll just wait and see. If they got it wrong we'll move down and test support in the short term," one trader said.
Recent cold weather in the U.S. prompted NYMEX heating oil to lead the complex up in the afternoon and heating oil held its strength through to the close.
Unrest in Nigeria where villagers in one of the country's oil producing regions took Royal Dutch/Shell workers hostage was not giving the market much support, traders said.

"There is so much crude around the temporary loss of 100,000 barrels per day is not enough to help. It would have to go on for a long time. Buyers in Europe are looking at begging sellers," one European refiner said.

April gas oil, which closed earlier up $1.50 at $172.25 after a quiet day's trading was called unchanged to slightly softer on the back of the Brent close. The product only partly followed the rise in heating oil prices and brokers expected it to continue to tie in closer to Brent crude.
"But if we see a large draw in heating oil that could all change," one added.
